abstract.p: Various kinematic performance measures have been proposed to quantify the optimality of manipulator configurations. Most performance criterh are based on maximizing the achievable range of motion or force at the endpoint, i.e. motion or force man@ulability. However, it is also important to consider the achievable amracy of motion and force control. Previous studies of accuracy have focused on the condition number of the Jacobian mat& We show that the condition number is not a true measure of accuracy, and that accuracy is inversely related to manipulability. The implkation of this result is that manipulability must be obtained at the expense of acwracy, and vice vetsa. The basic relationships between kinematic performance characteristics are examined. We characterize optimality as an appropriate compromise between manipulability and accuracy in both mofion and force. Kinematic optimization is formulated in terms of minimizing the deviation of the actual performance characteristics from a set of nominal characterbtics.
